validation_checks.name: Worst-case modifier stacking within caps
validation_checks.details: Coating pool worst-case: QT4(1.30) x scaffold(1.60) x shingle(1.40) x roughsawn(1.30) = 3.79x — under 4.0x cap. Prep pool worst-case: POOR(2.0) x RRP(2.0) x scaffold(1.60) x shingle(1.40) x roughsawn(1.30) = 11.65x — extreme theoretical (shingle + RRP + scaffold + roughsawn + POOR is unrealistic). Production.json includes T&M recommendation for any prep combination exceeding 4.0x. Realistic worst prep: FAIR(1.5) x no_RRP(1.0) x ladder(1.35) x lap(1.00) x cedarmill(1.15) = 2.33x — well within cap.

observations.description: Profile modifier values in production.json (panel=0.90, shingle=1.40) differ from resolution.json NC reference values (panel=1.10, shingle=2.00). Production engineer explicitly documents this as intentional RP calibration with detailed rationale: spray_backroll on panel is faster than lap (large flat runs ideal for backroll), and shingle penalty reduced from 2.00x to 1.40x because spray_backroll already carries a 25% penalty and handles edges better than spray-only. Accepted — production is authoritative for rate calibration.

Cedarmill texture modifier in production.json (1.15) differs from resolution.json reference (1.20). Production header MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING also uses 1.15. Minor calibration adjustment — production is authoritative.

PaintScope key PS_EXT_META.EA.CAULK_JOINTS uses 'EA' in namespace path but actual UOM is LF (input IN_LF_CAULK_JOINTS). The namespace prefix reflects PS category convention, not UOM, so this is not a functional error. Recommend renaming to PS_EXT_META.LF.CAULK_JOINTS for consistency in a future revision if the PS key catalog permits.

Production quality_tier_effects lists QT4 modifier as 1.30 but production modifier header worst_case_coating calculation uses QT4(1.30). Meanwhile resolution applicable_enums notes QT4=1.15 on qt_scaled tasks. The resolution QT4=1.15 and production QT4=1.30 are different — resolution says 1.15 is for qt_scaled tasks specifically, while production applies 1.30 to binary coating tasks. Both values are used correctly in their respective contexts: qt_scaled tasks have explicit QT4 rates built in, binary coating tasks use the 1.30 multiplier. Consistent in practice.

Research projected 42 tasks across 11 modules. Actual: 45 tasks across 8 modules. The delta (+3 tasks) is explained by SOP Librarian module consolidation (11 proposed modules merged to 8 per user instruction: separate CAULK, CLEAN, FINAL merged into PREP and CLEANUP) plus efflorescence assessment and caulk split into remove/apply adding tasks. Reasonable pipeline evolution.

SOP module MOD_FCRP_PREP lists required_input IN_LF_CAULK_JOINTS mapped to PS_EXT_META.EA.CAULK_JOINTS. Production siding_surface_input_group does NOT list this caulk input — it only lists 13 inputs (missing the caulk LF input). The caulk tasks in production (TSK_FCRP_CAULK_REMOVE_FAILED, TSK_FCRP_CAULK_APPLY_NEW) are LF-based and implicitly consume this input. Functional but not explicitly listed in the production input group.

change_log.author: Spec Critic
change_log.changes: Initial QA validation of SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_RP_v1. Clean PASS with zero issues and 6 minor observations. 45 tasks across 8 modules (7 owned MOD_FCRP_* + 1 shared MOD_RRP_EXT_CONTAINMENT), 6 material systems (2 RP-specific primers + 2 reused NC primers + 2 reused NC finishes), 5 coverage profiles, 20 consumables, 4 round configurations, 8 protection zones, 6 adjacent surfaces, 14 PaintScope inputs, 1 paintable item (ITM_SIDING_FIELD, SF-based), 7 configuration dimensions, 5 factor modifiers, 25 proposed registry additions. Context prefix FCRP unique. First exterior fiber cement siding RP spec. Combined assessment + prep + prime + finish. spray_backroll primary method. NO power washing — low-pressure rinse only.
